newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel oil barges steady, cargoe offers firm.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel oil barges steady, cargoe offers firm.

text.p: European high sulphur fuel barges quietly traded steady on Thursday with players standing back to assess the effect of the news that OPEC members had agreed to respect their production, while cargoes were offered a bit firmer.

Prompt high sulphur barges traded once at $83 a tonne fob ARA by midday, at the higher end of Wednesday's range, while a 1,000-tonne July barge was done at $83.75 a tonne, a touch less than a similar deal a day earlier.
"There is no bunker demand plus yesterday there was a good market with most people covering their shorts then," one trader said, putting Wednesday's total volume of trade at about 40,000 tonnes.
Barge demand by midday Thursday was 10,000 tonnes, he said.

Earlier in the day, July barges were offered a little firmer at $85 a tonne while dealers were said to be standing back to assess the effect on the market of the news that members of the oil cartel had pledged to respect their quotas allocations.
Bunkers were offered at $85.50/$86 for 380 CST material in Antwerp, traders said.
High sulphur cargoes were offered a little higher, with one seller saying his cracked material was on offer at $81/$81.50 while buying interest was said to be coming in at around the $79 mark.

Traders said 40,000 tonnes of cracked high sulphur were sold by a Scandinavian refiner late on Wednesday but some said it was done on a floating basis, at about high fob plus $3 while other traders said the cargo fetched a fixed $81.75 cif.
Russian high sulphur straight run was heard on offer at $84/$85 cif, a price deemed too high by some traders.
